About us

The NZ Super Fund invests money, on behalf of the New Zealand Government, to help pay for the increased cost of universal pension entitlements in the future. By doing this the Fund adds to Crown wealth, improves the ability of future Governments to pay for universal pensions, and ultimately reduces the tax burden on future New Zealanders. As a long-term, growth-oriented investor, the Fund has more than NZ$70 billion in assets. The Fund is managed by an Autonomous Crown Entity, the Guardians of New Zealand Superannuation.

    We've closed Growth Fund 7 at our $200m cap 👏 Coming up on 30 years backing Kiwi tech, with Movac's first investment back in 1998. General Partner Jason Graham sat down with NZ Herald NOW Business to talk through the raise. → One of the biggest votes of confidence in NZ tech this year, the raise landed nearly double its original first-close target before reaching cap. Backed by cornerstone investors including the Government Superannuation Fund Authority, Forsyth Barr Limited, Ngāi Tahu Holdings Corporation (a supporter since 2016), and NZ Super Fund (continuing a decade-long partnership with Movac). → The goal is never the exit. Jason put it simply: every founder and investor's job is to build the best business they can. An exit is sometimes the outcome, but it's never the point. → Staying a generalist investor is a New Zealand reality, not a strategy choice. At Movac's scale, Jason said you have to back a genuine mix, from PowerbyProxi's wireless charging tech (now in iPhones worldwide) to software companies like Vend, a Lightspeed Company, Unleashed Software and Timely. Thanks to everyone who's backed this raise, and to the founders doing the work that makes it worth backing. We have our first Growth Fund 7 investment locked in, and look forward to announcing details when we're able to. Watch the full interview below 👇 https://lnkd.in/e-UVGSKf Jason Graham Fi Foster Mark Stuart David Beard Mark Vivian Sabrine van Rossum Nathan Bell Millie McKelvie Byron van Vugt Emelie Verseput #MovacVC #G7 #GrowthFund7 #NZInvesting #HeraldNOWBusiness

    The legislation passed on Wednesday to establish a permitting regime for offshore renewable energy projects is a significant step towards giving New Zealand households and businesses access to a world-class fuel source: the country’s offshore wind. Over the past five years, we have invested some $15m into establishing the feasibility of developing a 1GW windfarm in the South Taranaki Bight and, provided the feasibility process is positive, we are on track to deliver the project in the early- to mid-2030s. Our proposed offshore wind farm will provide as much as seven typical onshore wind farms, or almost 7,500 hectares of solar panels. Those 4.5 terawatt hours per year connecting into the North Island network will reduce reliance on the Cook Strait cable, increase the impact of demand response, improve productivity for New Zealand industry, and inject new economic opportunities into the Taranaki region. They will also reduce the demand on the Southern hydro lakes to provide baseload power, allowing them to act as a giant battery and provide firming supply. We acknowledge the hard work of MBIE and the input of iwi, hapū and all community groups who have contributed to the process so far. Our vision is to bring offshore wind to New Zealand with broad community support and maximising benefits for the region and mana whenua. It was encouraging to hear politicians from all sides of the House recognising the economic benefits offshore wind could generate. We now look forward to continuing to work with the government to ensure a viable path to market exists for projects such as ours and that we are able to deliver long-term energy security for New Zealand.

    We're pleased to share that the NZ Super Fund has again been awarded a perfect score in Global SWF's GSR (Governance, Sustainability, and Resilience) Scoreboard. The annual assessment benchmarks best practise across the world's 200 largest sovereign wealth funds and public pension funds. This year, the Super Fund was one of just nine institutions to achieve a 100% score. Our CEO Jo Townsend said, "Global SWF’s scoreboard is a valuable guide to industry best practice for state-owned investors, and we are delighted to have performed well against these criteria again. It’s also pleasing to again see an increase in sustainability and resilience scores globally. Our discussions with peers show a strong ongoing commitment to these areas, in keeping with our shared focus on creating long-term value for stakeholders.” Designed to be fully independent, quantifiable and objective, the GSR Scoreboard ranks sovereign wealth funds and public pension funds against 25 criteria including transparency and accountability, governance, and sustainability and resilience. This is the third successive year the NZ Super Fund has received full marks.

    Global SWF

    🎂 Global SWF turns eight years old today, and to celebrate it, we have issued our latest #GSRscoreboard assessing best practices among SWFs and PPFs. 🏆 The system is independent, quantifiable, objective and dynamic - and has been updated and published for the past six years, always on July 1. ♻️ Three questions were changed this year to account for relative performance, carbon emission statements, and adoption of and/or investment in AI. 🔝 In a like-for-like comparison, the average GSR score of all 200 funds slightly increased to 60%. "S" and "R" scores improved, while "G" scores stayed flat. 🚨 Governments around the world, including those from deficit economies, continue to establish SWFs – role models and best practices become crucial. 🥇 In this context, we are delighted to announce the 9 perfect-scorers of 2026: - Norges Bank Investment Management 🇳🇴 - La Caisse (Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec) 🇨🇦 - Temasek 🇸🇬 - Future Fund 🇦🇺 - BCI 🇨🇦 - Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan 🇨🇦 - Rest 🇦🇺 - NZ Super Fund 🇳🇿 - NSIA: Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority 🇳🇬 Funds are arranged by size, but they are all winners - congratulations! https://lnkd.in/gd_Nsb3X

    New Zealand has this week won a global Climate Bonds Initiative award for the ‘Most Innovative Taxonomy' - great recognition for our country's reputation as a trusted destination for sustainable finance. The award recognises the leadership of the NZ Taxonomy Project in developing internationally-credible, evidence-based taxonomy criteria for the agriculture and forestry sectors. As secretariat of the NZ Taxonomy project, Centre for Sustainable Finance: Toitū Tahua, of which we are a founding member, accepted the award on behalf of partners and stakeholders. Congratulations to all involved.

    Centre for Sustainable Finance: Toitū Tahua

    3,569 followers

    1w

    The New Zealand Taxonomy project has just received the prestigious Climate Bonds Initiative Award for ‘Most Innovative Taxonomy’ at the #CONNECT conference at London Climate Action Week. While most taxonomy development is driven internationally, New Zealand's leadership in sustainable land use makes us well placed to innovate for agriculture and forestry. Developed with industry, scientists, Māori and financial sector representatives, and aligned with approaches emerging in Australia and Singapore, the NZ Taxonomy balances New Zealand's sector realities with international market expectations. This recognition by Climate Bonds, one of the world's leading sustainable finance certification bodies, reinforces the credibility of the NZ Taxonomy with international investors and markets. The NZ Taxonomy is a voluntary tool to help businesses and investors identify sustainable economic activities in New Zealand. As secretariat of the NZ Taxonomy project, CSF is pleased to have Jessica Desmond, pictured here with David Woods and Sean Kidney, accept the award on behalf of the project.     I’m delighted to announce that we’ve hit (and surpassed) the First Close of Movac Growth Fund 7, with $185m of investor commitments locked in. Our First Close target was $100m, but we’ve had huge demand and we will be closing the Fund within the next month at $200m. A sincere ‘Thank you’ to those investors who are investing, both new and existing Movac investors. And welcome to those #AIP investors who are now backing us and our companies going global. A special call-out to our cornerstone investors NZ Super Fund, Government Superannuation Fund Authority, Forsyth Barr Limited and Ngāi Tahu Holdings Corporation. Long term investor relationships are very important to us, and NZ Super has been a cornerstone of Movac growth funds for the past decade. NZ Super has consistently been one of the top performing sovereign wealth funds globally, and we’re fortunate and grateful to be the only NZ VC to have them as an investor. We have our first Growth Fund 7 investment locked in, and look forward to announcing details when we're able to. We’ve built significant experience (and scar tissue!) over almost 30 years, and appreciate what goes into building a successful, global tech business. We are keen to hear from companies looking for capital, skills and networks to help compound its growth and success so far. If you’re a founder/CEO whose tech firm has at least $2m in revenue, is experiencing rapid growth, and is looking to raise your Series A, B or beyond, now or in the next couple of years, DM me or any other Movac team member. We are writing cheques of $5m-30m plus, and able to lead or co-invest. We're able to provide a mix of primary and secondary capital via Growth Fund 7, or secondary capital only via our existing Growth Opportunity Fund 1. We've backed the teams at Auror, Re-Leased, Hnry, Dawn Aerospace, TracPlus, AutoGrab, LawVu, Vend, a Lightspeed Company, Alimetry, Unleashed Software, PowerbyProxi, Tradify, Aroa Biosurgery Limited, GreenButton Limited (Acquired by Microsoft) and Trade Me, across our various funds. Every VC firm has its own style, and what’s worked for us is investing in a pragmatic, disciplined way through various economic cycles, building concentrated fund portfolios where we can provide full support across a range of functional areas, as well as making peer connections across our various investee companies. We look forward to working with our Growth Fund 7 investors and the next wave of standout tech company founders, leaders and teams that we collectively back. Great to be back at the start line, again. Onwards. The INFINZ Board is offering 10 scholarships for senior finance students to attend the INFINZ Conference on 13 October 2026 at the Cordis, Auckland. This is a chance to connect with some of New Zealand's most senior financial services leaders, gain industry insight, and get a head start on your career. Who can apply? Full-time students at a New Zealand university (University of Auckland, Auckland University of Technology, University of Canterbury, Lincoln University (NZ), Massey University - Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa, University of Otago, Victoria University of Wellington, or The University of Waikato) studying a commerce-related degree including economics, finance, accounting, entrepreneurship, or commercial law. Priority given to final-year undergraduate and postgraduate students with grades of B+ or higher. Applicants must be current INFINZ members. Student membership starts from $20.     We're delighted to announce and introduce Lataai Tamaseu Russell, who has just been selected as our 2026 recipient of the NZ Super Fund AUT Business Scholarship - Pacific. This annual scholarship, in partnership with AUT Business School, has been set up to recognise and support an outstanding AUT student of Pacific descent in their penultimate year of a bachelor's degree in business.    Lataai shared with us about the moment she found out she got the scholarship and where her passion for business stems from.    "I was extremely surprised and very humbled to have received this scholarship. I have no doubt there are many students who would have been just as qualified, if not more to have received this scholarship, so it is an honour. Student fees build up over the years, so to know that I have been blessed with a scholarship that will cover my studies for a year will make a big difference.   "Business, especially finance and accounting feels like a different language, and not everyone in our Pasifika community has had the chance to learn it. By studying finance and accounting, I’m learning that language so I can share it with my own parents, my children, and communities who want to build a better financial future. Studying business is an opportunity to help others to have stronger financial futures." We're so proud of your achievements and congratulations on your deserving recognition, Lataai!
